sections.h2: How quickly can a Yorktown house change hands?
sections.html:
The usual paths are a broker listing, a private sale, or a cash buyer who takes the house as it is. Yorktown is a town on the northern edge of Westchester County, about 38 miles north of midtown Manhattan, so a seller works with the town's tax receiver, assessor and building inspector instead of a city hall.

The town is made up of five business hamlets, and no train runs inside its borders. Buyers weigh commute time, school district and the age of the mechanical systems, which makes the records you can hand over early the main factor in closing speed.

sections.h2: What is the profile of Yorktown households?
sections.html:
Owners dominate, incomes are high and the population has eased down slightly. The federal estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,944 people, 1.7 percent below the 2020 base of 36,562.

Nearly 95 percent of residents stayed put over the past year, so many owners have long tenures. Commuters head to the nearest Metro-North stations, in Katonah on the Harlem Line and Peekskill on the Hudson Line.

sections.h2: Where is Yorktown, and what are its hamlets?
sections.html:
Putnam Valley in Putnam County bounds the town on the north, Somers on the east, New Castle on the south and Cortlandt on the west. Total area is 39.3 square miles, of which about 36.8 are land. The Croton River crosses the south end and was dammed there to give New York City its first major supply of clean water.

Early records call the area Hanover. The township took the Yorktown name in 1788 to honor the 1781 victory at Yorktown, Virginia. Population stood at 4,731 in 1950, reached 16,453 by 1960 and has hovered around 36,000 since 2000.

  • Yorktown Heights, the mailing address of Town Hall.
  • Jefferson Valley, site of the Jefferson Valley Mall.
  • Shrub Oak, Mohegan Lake and Crompond, part of which lies in Cortlandt.

Notable employers and landmarks include the IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center in the Kitchawan area and the headquarters of PCSB Bank in Yorktown Heights. Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park and the North County Trailway, built on the old New York and Putnam rail bed, are the best known open spaces.

Four districts reach into the town, and the one on your bill sets your school levy. The Yorktown Central School District covers a large part of the town, with the Lakeland Central, Croton-Harmon Union Free and Ossining Union Free districts handling the remainder.

The town receiver collects school tax on behalf of all four but has no say over their budgets. Confirm the district before you list, and tell buyers which one applies.

sections.h2: How do winters and storms affect an older Yorktown house?
sections.html:
Weather records for Yorktown Heights show about 50.3 inches of precipitation and 39.5 inches of snow in a year. January lows average 16.7 degrees, the coldest reading on record is minus 15, and the hottest is 100.

Snow load, repeated freezing and thawing and long cold spells put the roof, driveway and heating plant at the top of an inspection list. A house with a recent furnace and roof, and the receipts to show it, will present better than one without.

sections.h2: How do Yorktown tax bills and penalties work?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes collects what the town levies, including fire, parks, sewer and water districts, together with county and school tax. Owners receive two bills a year, and a bill that fails to arrive does not cancel the obligation.

  • School tax, July 1 to June 30: one bill is mailed September 1 with two stubs. Half is due September 30 and half January 31, and a weekend due date rolls to the next business day, which puts the 2027 second half on February 1.
  • School penalties on the first half: 2 percent in October, 5 percent in November, 7 percent in December and January, 10 percent in February and March, 12 percent afterward until sale.
  • Town and county tax: mailed April 1, due April 30. Penalties run 2 percent in May, 5 percent in June and July, 7 percent in August and September, 10 percent from October through December and 12 percent after that.

The second school half draws no penalty through January and 10 percent in February and March. No reminder notices go out in January, and the town has no authority to waive penalties. A mailed payment needs a genuine post office postmark by the due date, and since December 24, 2025 machine postmarks reflect the day mail is first processed at a regional facility, so mail well ahead. The Tax Office at 363 Underhill Avenue keeps weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and a green drop box sits behind Town Hall.

sections.h2: How do you grieve a Yorktown assessment?
sections.html:
Applications are accepted from June 1 through Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of June. For the 2027 roll the cutoff is 8 p.m. on June 15, 2027, and the Board of Assessment Review sits at Town Hall that evening from 4 to 8 p.m. Filing is free and needs no attorney.

Support your case with sales of similar houses in your neighborhood and school district within a year of the July 1, 2026 valuation date, or with an appraisal. Email filings are refused. Hand-delivery, mail, FedEx, UPS and the drop box at the rear entrance of Town Hall are accepted, and the board mails its determination on September 15, 2027.

The assessor also examines each transfer of property, noting buyer, seller and price. Common exemptions include senior citizens, STAR, veterans and agricultural. Call 914-962-5722, extension 2.

sections.h2: What does the Yorktown Building Department oversee?
sections.html:
The Building Inspector applies the town's zoning ordinance and the State building codes, writes permits and certificates of occupancy, and can authorize condemnation of unsafe buildings. The 2025 editions of the State codes took effect December 31, 2025, and any application filed on or after that day is measured against them. Hours are weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The town warns that it never tells anyone to wire a development fee. Fees are paid by check to the Town of Yorktown under the master fee schedule.

sections.h2: How is a Yorktown deed recorded, and what does the state charge?
sections.html:
The Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division handles recording. It wants a recording cover page, a TP-584, an RP-5217 and a payment cover page, all prepared in the clerk's PREP portal.

As an illustration, the $606,800 typical home value rounds up to $607,000, which makes 1,214 units of $500 and a state tax of $2,428, payable when the deed is presented. A residence at $1 million or more adds a 1 percent buyer's tax.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Yorktown school tax due?
faqs.a: January 31. A weekend date moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due Monday, February 1.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to Yorktown town and county tax paid in June?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent. The bill is due April 30, adds 2 percent in May and 5 percent in June and July, and the town says it cannot waive any of it.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Yorktown assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Assessment Office between June 1 and Grievance Day, which is June 15, 2027, attaching comparable sales or an appraisal. The office does not take email filings.

faqs.q: Which Yorktown office issues certificates of occupancy?
faqs.a: The Building Department at Town Hall, 363 Underhill Avenue, headed by the Building Inspector, who also issues permits and enforces zoning and State codes.

faqs.q: What would state transfer tax be on a $606,800 Yorktown sale?
faqs.a: It would be $2,428, because the price rounds up to $607,000. The seller pays unless the contract shifts it to the buyer.
